paper.title: Social class and (un)ethical behaviour: Causal and correlational evidence

claims.claim: The two main survey experiments include more than 11,000 participants; the article reports 4,785 completed Survey1 experiments, 6,243 Survey2 participants, and 807 belief-survey respondents.
claims.exhibit: Abstract and main text, Sections 1 and 4

claims.claim: Survey1 sample characteristics by priming condition reproduce Table 1 descriptive statistics.
Survey2 sample characteristics by treatment reproduce Table 2 descriptive statistics.
Survey1 manipulation-check means and sample sizes reproduce Table 3.
Survey1 payment means, sample sizes, and regression estimates reproduce Tables 4 and 5.
Survey2 manipulation-check means and sample sizes reproduce Table 6.
Survey2 payment means and sample sizes reproduce Table 7.
Beliefs and moral-judgement descriptive results reproduce Table 9.
Payment distribution tests reported in the text reject uniform/random payment frequencies except the stated €14 Survey1 and €16 Survey2 bins.
Survey1 reported balance comparisons and priming contrasts are consistent with the computed Wilcoxon tests.
Survey2 reported priming contrasts and absence of significant payment differences are consistent with computed tests.

findings.description: Survey2 Stata cleaning recodes the €4,500–€5,000 income interval to €4,275. This lowers the computed Table 2 income means relative to the printed values.
findings.evidence: B_DataCleaning_Survey2.do line: replace income = 4275 if income_interval == 11; Supplementary-Survey2.Rmd uses 4750 for q37==11. R translation mean is €2,258.57 in primed-rich vs printed €2,271.0, and €2,214.81 vs €2,227.0 in primed-poor.
findings.suggested_fix: Author should resolve the interval-11 value in shipped Stata code and document the intended midpoint; any correction is outside this reproduction.

findings.description: Several printed regression cells differ from the direct R translation at their displayed precision.
findings.evidence: Table 5 model (2) real-rich coefficient: −0.245 printed versus −0.2542 computed. Table 5 model (4) male robust SE: 0.25 versus 0.2551. Table 8 model (4) R2: 0.006 versus 0.00750.
findings.suggested_fix: Review the affected table cells or the original Stata run output; the translation retained shipped specifications and samples.

findings.description: SurveyBelief Table 9 values include small discrepancies; most are consistent with truncation to the displayed precision.
findings.evidence: The belief-extent means are 4.826, 4.987, and 4.691 (full, rich, poor); the printed group values include 4.8, 4.9, and 4.6. The computed extent SDs truncate to 1.58, 1.5, and 1.61.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify Table 9 summaries against the authors’ original Stata output and clarify rounding convention.

findings.description: The Survey1 source-wave build script cannot be run because its required GIP wave input files are not shipped; the active main file comments out this build and uses the provided anonymized master dataset.
findings.evidence: A_MainFile_Survey1.do comments out B_CreateMasterDataSet.do; waves 25, 31, and 37 are absent from the package.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide the restricted source waves or preserve the documented anonymized-file workflow.

findings.description: The text overstates how many payment-bin tests have p<.01.
findings.evidence: The R exact binomial translation gives p=.0119 for Survey1 €6; for Survey2 it gives p=.0128 for €2, .0262 for €4, and .0309 for €18, although the article says only the €14/€16 bin is an exception.
findings.suggested_fix: Recheck the relevant binomial test output and correct the text or test values.
